backend-services/routes/endpoint_routes..notes: All endpoint CRUD, listing, validation, and validation-alias routes are mapped to native Rust. Core endpoints match typed-model validation, create/update/delete permissions and route-specific denial codes, authenticated reads/listing, missing-item/list errors, immutable identity checks, duplicate/client-URI checks, and CRUD responses. Endpoint-validation service error semantics and a few exceptional storage envelopes remain incomplete.

backend-services/routes/monitor_routes.p.notes: Liveness, readiness, metrics, and CSV report routes plus their helper behavior are implemented natively. Readiness now matches Python's always-200 degraded contract and declared public/privileged response shapes while retaining descriptor checks. Metrics aggregation and report sections are present, but exact range/group/sort aggregation, Python date parsing, log-backed report reconstruction, daily bandwidth rows, and dynamic filenames remain incomplete.

backend-services/routes/gateway_routes.p.notes: The public health/status/cache operations and REST, SOAP, GraphQL, gRPC, HEAD, and preflight entry points are all native Rust routes. Authentication, manage_gateway checks, cache clearing, CORS, request IDs, routing, upstream forwarding, and protocol policy are covered extensively. The monolithic Python gateway implementation is distributed across Rust protocol/policy modules, and every exceptional fallback and duplicate legacy gRPC definition has not yet been mapped statement-for-statement.

backend-services/routes/config_routes.py.notes: All export, import, snapshot, upsert, and rollback routes/helpers are implemented natively. Rust now matches granular export/import permission codes, single-resource response keys and CFG404-CFG407 misses, API pair selection, endpoint filters, malformed-entry handling, snapshots, and the pinned rollback error/success envelopes. Storage transactions are intentionally stronger than Python's sequential writes, and exact datetime representation plus every partial-write failure mode are not 1:1.

backend-services/routes/credit_routes.py.notes: All credit-definition, user-credit, retrieval, and key-rotation routes are mapped to native Rust. Definition management now matches manage_credits gates, masked response fields, default paginated list shape, CRD021 misses, typed models, CRUD errors, and user-credit retrieval permissions. Exact query pagination/search, the Python path-username shadowing bug, encrypted key rotation/creation semantics, and some database-specific error envelopes remain incomplete.

backend-services/routes/proto_routes.py.notes: Proto validation, upload/update/get/delete, descriptor compilation/persistence, package extraction, and descriptor backfill are implemented natively without generated Python modules. Rust now matches operation-specific AUTH001/API008 permission errors, case-insensitive filename extension handling, Python's ignored client filename, retrieval message/API002 miss, update message, nullable descriptor deletion, and delete-always-success behavior. Filesystem archive/package-init helpers are obsolete in the native runtime, while exact compiler diagnostics and every validation error string remain incomplete.

backend-services/routes/tools_routes.py.notes: The CORS checker, gRPC environment report, and backend chaos controls are implemented natively. Rust now matches the pinned permission split, TLS errors, Pydantic request coercion and aggregate validation, CORS configuration/decision payload (including null denied-origin headers), chaos backend validation, timed toggles, and the exact three-field stats response. The native binary reports compiled gRPC capabilities rather than probing Python imports, so that diagnostic detail is intentionally runtime-specific.

backend-services/routes/openapi_routes.p.notes: All four OpenAPI discovery routes and both helpers are implemented natively. Rust now matches manage_apis/manage_endpoints boundaries, route-specific errors and messages, ordered multi-server fetching, parsed endpoint shape, cached reads, refresh summary responses, fetch-on-import behavior, duplicate skipping, description truncation, and parse previews. Rust persists fetched specs with the API record instead of using Python's process-local one-hour cache, and exact malformed nested-spec exceptions/storage failure envelopes remain incomplete.

backend-services/routes/memory_routes.py.notes: Both encrypted memory dump/restore routes and optional request models are implemented natively. Rust matches manage_security gates and SEC codes, memory-mode and key checks, Pydantic path validation/coercion, encrypted round trips, response nesting, missing-file handling, and generic failure envelopes. Rust deliberately restricts snapshot paths to the configured dump directory rather than accepting arbitrary filesystem paths, so path-policy behavior is not 1:1.

backend-services/routes/role_routes.py.notes: All role CRUD/list aliases and administrator-visibility checks are implemented natively. Rust now matches authenticated permission-free reads, operation-specific ROLE009/010/011 denials, ROLE013-016 administrator protections, legacy platform_admin detection, service ROLE001/004/005 errors, sorted pagination metadata, non-admin filtering, Pydantic model normalization, and CRUD responses. Exact malformed integer query validation and exceptional cache/database failure envelopes remain incomplete.

backend-services/routes/analytics_routes.notes: All seven analytics endpoints and top-pair normalization are implemented natively. Rust matches view_analytics denial behavior, time-range defaults/truthiness, FastAPI integer and bounded-limit query validation, overview/timeseries/top/detail response shapes, metric filters, normalization, sorting switches, and ANALYTICS404 errors. Native aggregate counters are not yet fully time-range scoped, endpoint latency/percentiles are placeholders, and Python's exact granularity rebucketing and snapshot percentile calculations remain incomplete.

backend-services/routes/quota_routes.py.notes: All quota response models, dependency behavior, status/history/export/tier/burst routes, and quota calculations are mapped to native Rust. Rust matches tier fallback, the pinned expired-assignment override quirk, request and bandwidth quota keys, thresholds, response fields, request-only exports, CSV formatting, upgrade filtering, HTTP detail errors, and reset boundaries. Burst usage remains zero because the native tier limiter does not yet persist Python-compatible :burst counters, and exact tracker graceful-degradation/storage exception behavior remains incomplete.

backend-services/routes/rate_limit_rule_.notes: All request/response models, CRUD/actions, search, bulk operations, duplication, statistics, and declared status behavior are mapped to native Rust. Rust matches Pydantic coercion and VAL001 handling, public management exposure, enum/value errors, priority ordering, memory-backend regex behavior, source/duplicate errors, legacy enabled counting, and the pinned Starlette route-shadowing defects for status and bulk actions. Exact external Mongo cursor/update failure behavior and the unreachable authenticated status handler's internal service query are not fully reproduced.

backend-services/routes/tier_routes.py.notes: All tier limit/request/response models and every CRUD, assignment, lifecycle action, comparison, user-list, and statistics route are mapped to native Rust. Rust now matches the pinned public boundary (only listing and statistics enforce manage_tiers), idempotent creation, search failure quirk, assignment replacement/null fields, serialized-effective-date failures, tier fallback, lifecycle notes/status codes, deletion safeguards, and statistics shapes. Exact Pydantic coercion for every nested tier model, some malformed query/body envelopes, service cache behavior, and exceptional database fallbacks remain incomplete.

backend-services/utils/email_util.py.notes: Rust provides the same always-successful mock email logger and tier lifecycle actions invoke it with the pinned recipients, subjects, bodies, and payment-failure follow-up notification.

backend-services/utils/group_util.py.notes: Rust resolves the authenticated user and API before enforcing the same non-empty group intersection and 401 detail across REST, SOAP, GraphQL, and gRPC. The monolithic evaluator replaces Python's path parsing/cache lookup, but exact malformed-path and missing-user exception fallbacks are not fully identical.

backend-services/utils/shared_metrics_ut.notes: Rust records the same Redis minute-bucket fields and native monitor responses merge in-process gateway counters. Cross-process Redis bucket merging into monitor snapshots, including Python's exact day grouping, top-list merge, unique-user overcount, and fail-open scan behavior, is not yet implemented.

backend-services/utils/subscription_util.notes: Rust enforces the same authentication, admin bypass default, protocol API/version resolution, 403 detail, and subscription-list membership. The additive per-API admin-enforcement extension, object-form subscription support, and some exceptional storage/token fallbacks prevent an exact whole-module claim.

backend-services/utils/error_util.py.notes: Rust constructs the same request-id-aware success and error envelopes throughout the control plane and converts policy failures for every data-plane protocol. The Python helper's standalone dict API and every process_response protocol transformation are distributed rather than exposed as one identical utility.

backend-services/utils/paging_util.py.notes: Rust now preserves the MAX_PAGE_SIZE default, blank/invalid fallback, minimum-one coercion, one-based validation, and exact bound messages at management list boundaries. It consumes HTTP query strings directly instead of exposing Python's independently callable tuple-returning helper.

backend-services/utils/api_resolution_ut.notes: The pinned module is dead production code, but native GraphQL and gRPC handlers implement required-version validation, API name/version policy paths, and storage resolution. Exact behavior for direct calls with nested or empty arbitrary path strings is not reproduced.

backend-services/utils/api_util.py.notes: Rust policy document loading resolves APIs by name/version or ID, locates endpoint documents by client/endpoint URI, and maintains shared routing state. Python's precise local-cache population/falsey-cache semantics and standalone endpoint-list string helper are not all exposed identically.

backend-services/utils/credit_util.py.notes: Rust atomically deducts credits, resolves user and definition headers, decrypts legacy enc: values, and implements old/new key rotation timing. Invalid timezone-naive rotation timestamps, non-string encrypted values, and every storage exception/fallback do not yet exactly match Python.

backend-services/utils/encryption_util.p.notes: Rust implements TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY/MEM_ENCRYPTION_KEY precedence, Fernet-key validation with SHA-256 URL-safe derivation fallback, plaintext compatibility, enc: marking, and fail-closed decryption. Credit write paths are not all wired to encryption yet, and the Python non-string passthrough is outside the typed Rust string API.

backend-services/utils/password_util.py.notes: Rust uses bcrypt for hash/verify and now counts Unicode characters while accepting Unicode uppercase, lowercase, and numeric characters under the pinned password policy. Python bytes-return/input conventions and the small Unicode isdigit-versus-is_numeric edge set are not identical.

backend-services/utils/routing_util.py.notes: Rust preserves client-routing over endpoint over API precedence, per-key round robin, endpoint client_uri lookup, and shared cache indices. Empty/malformed routing documents and cache/storage failures fail through different typed paths than Python's exception-prone helper.

backend-services/utils/audit_util.py.notes: Rust emits structured management and IP audit events and now matches Python's recursive sensitive-key exception rules plus JWT, authorization, API-key, hex, and private-key value redaction. Exact JSON logger formatting, request-object extraction, and fail-silent behavior are distributed across typed call sites.

backend-services/utils/cache_manager_uti.notes: The aiocache decorator factory is initialized and attached to FastAPI state but is never consumed by pinned production code; Rust uses its native shared storage/cache implementation directly.
backend-services/utils/cache_manager_uti.rationale: Unused FastAPI/aiocache framework adapter made obsolete with removal of the Python application runtime.

backend-services/utils/gateway_utils.py.notes: Rust preserves the sensitive-header denylist, CR/LF/NUL and HTML-tag removal, 8192-character truncation marker, case-insensitive allowlist, and never-forwards-sensitive behavior. Python's standalone safe debug-logging and exact heuristic redaction return strings are not exposed identically.

backend-services/utils/vault_encryption_.notes: Rust derives the same PBKDF2-SHA256 Fernet key from email, username, and VAULT_KEY, emits v1: ciphertext, accepts prefixed or legacy unprefixed ciphertext, decrypts values, and reports configuration state. Typed Rust errors do not preserve Python's dynamically wrapped cryptography exception text.

backend-services/services/subscription_s.notes: Rust preserves API existence checks, subscription retrieval including the empty-list special case, subscribe/unsubscribe mutation, cache-backed shared state, request-id errors, messages, and SUB003-SUB006 contracts through native routes.

backend-services/utils/grpc_util.py.notes: Rust natively encodes and decodes big-endian gRPC-Web data/trailer frames, handles split streaming output, and implements the pinned empty reflection fallback within full descriptor-backed gRPC support. The standalone Python parser's incomplete-buffer discard and duplicate default/custom trailer-line quirks are not reproduced byte-for-byte.

backend-services/utils/health_check_util.notes: Rust checks configured Mongo/Redis health, reports process memory, formats uptime identically, and supplies all detailed gateway status fields. active_connections currently reports active gateway requests instead of psutil network socket count, and OS inspection failure fallbacks differ.

backend-services/utils/ip_policy_util.py.notes: Rust matches trusted-proxy resolution, XFF precedence, exact/CIDR/netmask matching, blacklist precedence, whitelist errors, Docker loopback addresses, and per-API trust overrides. Rust intentionally does not let a spoofable Host header alone trigger localhost bypass, and its typed audit/error plumbing differs from Python's broad fail-open catches.

backend-services/services/api_service.py.notes: Rust maps all API service operations to native CRUD with idempotent creation, generated IDs/paths, public-credit rejection, immutable identity, cache-backed storage, pagination metadata, proto descriptor attachment, and pinned API002/API003/API005/API006/API013 responses. Acknowledgement/cursor failure envelopes and a few cache-warming side effects remain incomplete.

backend-services/services/routing_servic.notes: Rust preserves generated client keys, duplicate handling, immutable-key checks, CRUD messages/errors, normalized documents, sorted pagination metadata, and shared-cache invalidation through native routing routes.

backend-services/services/vault_service..notes: Rust preserves all user lookup, email/configuration validation, duplicate handling, encrypted persistence, secret suppression, timestamps, description-only updates, no-change success, deletion, and VAULT001-VAULT008 response behavior.

backend-services/utils/chaos_util.py.notes: Rust has thread-safe Redis/Mongo outage flags, duration-based automatic clearing, an atomic error-budget counter, stats, and matching management routes. The flags are not yet consulted by native storage operations, so toggling them does not reproduce Python's injected backend failures.

backend-services/utils/sanitize_util.py.notes: Rust implements the pinned HTML escaping/tag stripping, whitespace and NUL normalization, character-count truncation, dangerous URL-scheme rejection, control-character removal, and ASCII username/API-name allowlists as typed utilities.

backend-services/services/group_service..notes: Rust preserves group existence checks, duplicate/create/update/delete/get behavior, immutable names, no-op and empty updates, cache-backed shared storage, sorted pagination metadata, messages, and GRP001-GRP007 errors.

backend-services/services/role_service.p.notes: Rust preserves role existence checks, duplicate/create/update/delete/get behavior, immutable names, applied no-op updates, returned updated records, shared-cache state, sorted pagination metadata, messages, and ROLE001-ROLE008 errors.

backend-services/utils/bandwidth_util.py.notes: Rust preserves window aliases/defaults, bucket keys, shared current usage, request-plus-response byte accounting, disabled/zero/missing-user bypass, and the pinned used-at-limit or content-length-over-limit 429 boundary. Storage failures are fail-closed in native external mode rather than Python's best-effort local fallback.

backend-services/utils/role_util.py.notes: Rust strips storage IDs, recognizes platform_admin plus legacy admin names, resolves admin users, and performs role permission checks for every pinned action. Typed storage failures return false directly, so Python's intermediate cache warming and validate_platform_role 404-to-500 exception quirk are not reproduced everywhere.

backend-services/utils/auth_util.py.notes: Rust implements JWT configuration detection, positive expiry parsing and unit aliases, CSRF double-submit/cache fallback, cookie and bearer extraction, kid-based key selection, signature/claim/revocation/user checks, active-user enforcement, permission claims, UUID jti, and access/refresh expiry. Some backend-outage detail mappings, testserver HTTPS heuristics, and legacy helper return conventions remain incomplete.

backend-services/utils/limit_throttle_ut.notes: Rust preserves duration aliases/defaults, expiring shared counters, user rate-limit boundaries, throttle activation/count/queue/excess rules, dynamic wait scaling, IP bucketing, retry headers/body, disable flag, and cache reset. Python's process-local fallback after Redis errors and test-runtime minimum-sleep branches are intentionally absent from production-native enforcement.

backend-services/utils/memory_log.py.notes: Rust now records every formatted structured event into a thread-safe 50,000-line ring buffer, returns copied snapshots, stores compatible time/name/level/message JSON records, and merges recent memory records into native log queries/exports.

backend-services/utils/wsdl_util.py.notes: Rust provides XXE/DTD-safe WSDL parsing and validation, service/namespace/operation/action/endpoint extraction, SOAP 1.1/1.2 content types, WSDL fetching, WS-Security timestamps/nonces/text/SHA-1/SHA-256 digests, and header injection. XML serialization whitespace/prefix choices and exact fetch/parser exception strings are not byte-identical.

backend-services/utils/graphql_util.py.notes: Rust now matches Python's line-comment and quote stripping, brace depth, regex word complexity, keyword removal, depth limits, introspection fetching, schema operation/type extraction, and subscription discovery within native GraphQL routes. Some malformed schema shapes and standalone network failure return paths remain distributed rather than identical helper calls.

backend-services/utils/key_util.py.notes: Rust supports JWT_KEYS list/wrapper/single-object forms, HS256 and RS256, inline and file-backed RSA verification/signing keys, active signing selection, explicit kid verification including inactive rotation keys, single-key no-kid fallback, legacy-key fallback, and JWT_SECRET_KEY compatibility. Python's five-minute process cache and development import-time DEFAULT_DEV_KEY snapshot are not reproduced.

backend-services/services/endpoint_servi.notes: Rust preserves endpoint and endpoint-validation CRUD, immutable identity fields, duplicate/client-URI conflict detection, API linkage, pagination, masking of storage internals, permissions, and the principal END00x response contracts. Python-only pre-generation of Python gRPC modules is not reproduced, and a few endpoint-validation storage failure codes remain consolidated by the native route layer.

backend-services/services/logging_servic.notes: Rust reads file and in-memory structured logs, now continues to the ring buffer when the log directory is absent, parses legacy text records, derives Python-compatible request/user/IP/endpoint/timing/status/type fields, applies date/time, case-insensitive substring, status, timing and exclusion filters, paginates newest-first, computes dashboard statistics, and exports JSON/CSV. File discovery is intentionally bounded and native export/read failure handling is not identical in every filesystem edge case.

backend-services/services/credit_service.notes: Rust preserves credit-definition validation/CRUD/masking, definition and per-user pagination/search, user-credit upsert/read behavior, and key rotation. Credit definition keys and per-user keys are now encrypted on every write with the compatible field cipher, decrypted only for authorized user-credit reads, and rotation stores user_api_key while creating a missing user record as Python does. Some database-driver-specific error distinctions remain consolidated by shared storage.

backend-services/services/rate_limit_rul.notes: Rust preserves rate-limit rule create/get/list/update/delete, enable/disable, duplicate, priority ordering, filters, case-insensitive search fields, statistics, validation, timestamps, and the pinned router's observable bulk/status shadowing defects. Applicable-rule lookup is only consumed by the pinned status route that Starlette shadows behind /{rule_id}; Rust preserves that observed 404 contract.

backend-services/services/crud_service.p.notes: Rust preserves dynamic collection selection, REST list/get/create/update/delete contracts, UUID generation, partial updates, GraphQL CRUD operations, SOAP discovery/execution/faults, and proto discovery, while adding native gRPC and gRPC-Web execution. CRUD validation now matches Python required/type behavior (including bool as int/number), nested required fields, string lengths/patterns/enums, numeric bounds, and detailed error lists. Generated discovery document formatting and some exceptional non-object payload paths are not byte-identical.

backend-services/services/user_service.p.notes: Rust preserves username/email lookup and password stripping, bandwidth usage/reset enrichment, duplicate and custom-attribute validation, Unicode-aware password policy and bcrypt hashing, update/delete/password response contracts, Python's role-change subscription purge iteration behavior, and sorted paginated user listing. Native routes also enforce v2 super-admin and self-update protections, while cache and database-driver-specific failure distinctions are consolidated.

backend-services/utils/transform_util.py.notes: Rust preserves request/response header, JSON body, array JSONPath, query, wrap/remove/rename/set, and status transformations in the native proxy. Scalar header/query additions now use Python-compatible True/False/None spelling and status maps accept numeric strings. The unused Python TransformError and validate_transform_config helpers have no direct native call equivalents, and invalid HTTP header material is skipped at the typed HeaderMap boundary.

backend-services/utils/hot_reload_config.notes: Rust supports the same 22 reloadable keys, JSON/YAML loading, nested-key flattening, environment precedence, scalar parsing, SIGHUP and authenticated HTTP reload, configuration dumps, and live gateway timeout/retry changes. Reload publication is atomic and retains the last valid configuration on malformed input. Python's generic in-process set/callback API is not used outside this module; dynamic LOG_LEVEL application and most advertised keys still require restart in Rust and are reported as such by the API.

backend-services/utils/http_client.py.notes: Rust provides shared asynchronous upstream clients, configurable connect/read timeouts, per-API read overrides, retry counts, transient 500/502/503/504 and network retry behavior, jittered capped exponential backoff, retry/timeout metrics, and closed/open/half-open circuit transitions. Timeout metrics now count each timed-out attempt as Python does. Reqwest does not expose separate Python httpx write/pool timeout controls, and network exception classes map through native client errors.

backend-services/utils/demo_seed_util.py.notes: Rust now implements configurable randomized roles, groups, users with bcrypt passwords, APIs, endpoints, encrypted credit definitions, user credits, subscriptions, log files, proto fixtures, metrics, deterministic seeds, and collection-count results, in addition to the admin-only memory-mode demo endpoint. The seeded Rust RNG is reproducible but does not reproduce CPython's Mersenne Twister byte-for-byte, and the compact native analytics aggregator records generated metrics in the current minute rather than reconstructing 400 historical Python MinuteBucket timestamps.

backend-services/utils/doorman_cache_asy.notes: The pinned async cache manager is not imported by production code; it exists for standalone compatibility tests. Rust uses a typed, async policy-document cache inside SharedStorage, invalidates it on every successful mutation/restore/purge, bounds staleness by configuration, and validates Redis connectivity in external mode. Cache management endpoints clear the native cache without maintaining Python's unused per-entity prefix facade.
backend-services/utils/doorman_cache_asy.rationale: Unused Python async Redis/memory compatibility facade made obsolete by the native shared-storage policy cache.

backend-services/utils/database_async.py.notes: Rust provides native async memory/MongoDB storage, startup connectivity validation, dynamic CRUD collections, unique indexes for the same core identities, admin/role/group initialization, environment-required admin password hashing, admin UI access, and graceful client ownership. The Python Motor facade, sync-memory wrapper classes, dotenv import behavior, and exported collection globals are language-specific; native external mode also validates its Redis dependency during the same connection phase.

backend-services/utils/async_db.py.notes: Rust storage calls are async at the SharedStorage boundary and expose native find-one/find-many/insert/update/delete operations across memory, MongoDB, and PostgreSQL backends. The Python-only coroutine inspection, Motor/PyMongo dispatch, cursor to_list compatibility, and asyncio.to_thread shim have no role after removal of Python database drivers.
backend-services/utils/async_db.py.rationale: Language- and driver-specific async compatibility adapter made obsolete by Rust's typed async storage layer.

backend-services/utils/memory_dump_util..notes: Rust implements the Python-compatible DMP1 format using HKDF-SHA256 and AES-256-GCM, timestamped naming, exact-file management restores, latest-file startup discovery, memory-only enforcement, atomic restore, version validation, and encrypted unsanitized state. Restore now decodes Python byte wrappers (including bcrypt hashes) and reapplies bootstrap-admin email/password/UI environment policy. Python's generic conversion of non-JSON arbitrary objects and byte-valued dictionary keys has no equivalent in the typed JSON storage model.

backend-services/utils/auth_blacklist.py.notes: Rust stores revoke-all and per-JTI records in the configured shared storage, validates unsafe multi-worker memory configurations, enforces revoke-all until explicit clear, applies TTLs, ignores expired or malformed JTI records at request time, and periodically purges expired records. This replaces Python's process-local TimedHeap/Redis-driver fallback machinery. Native bulk purge currently preserves malformed or missing-expiry JTI rows in external storage even though request-time checks safely ignore them.

backend-services/utils/security_settings.notes: Rust preserves environment/default merging, database-over-file precedence, memory-mode file restore, initial persistence, partial settings updates, cached runtime propagation, configurable autosave cadence, and settings-file mirroring. The native worker reacts to settings changes without task restart, uses atomic owner-only file writes, and honors enable_auto_save; pinned Python's loop inadvertently dumps whenever memory mode and frequency are set even when enable_auto_save is false.

backend-services/utils/enhanced_metrics_.notes: Rust records minute-bucket request/error/latency/byte totals, global status/API/user/endpoint counters, retry and timeout runtime counters, bounded retention, persistence/restore, range summaries, top entities, status distributions, and multi-level range output. Native buckets currently retain weighted latency averages rather than every raw latency sample, so percentile and per-endpoint latency output is approximate; top/status entity counters are process-global rather than reconstructed per requested range.

backend-services/utils/metrics_util.py.notes: Rust records minute request/error/latency/byte totals, status/API/user counters, persists and restores the Python JSON bucket format atomically, retains the Python MetricsStore 30-day maximum, and now honors monitor range, minute/day grouping, and ascending/descending series ordering with Python field names and weighted daily averages. Native compact buckets do not retain raw latency samples, per-bucket status/API/user maps, test-request counts, or per-bucket retry/timeout counts, so p95 and some range-scoped breakdowns remain approximate or zero.

backend-services/utils/analytics_aggrega.notes: Rust retains minute metrics for the longer 30-day MetricsStore contract and aggregates range-query output into Python's five-minute (up to 24h), hourly (up to 7d), and daily (longer) levels, preserving request/error/byte totals and request-weighted latency. Native state does not persist three duplicate rollup deques, and its compact points do not retain Python's raw-latency percentile samples or per-bucket unique-user sets.

backend-services/utils/analytics_schedul.notes: Rust starts an interval-driven metrics autosave task, restores persisted metrics at startup, writes atomically through the analytics store, and retains minute points for the 30-day MetricsStore contract. It does not maintain Python's separate scheduled five-minute, hourly, and daily deques; native analytics queries aggregate the retained minute series on demand.

backend-services/utils/quota_tracker.py.notes: Rust preserves calendar month/day counter keys, quota availability, remaining usage, fractional percentages, 80/95 percent warning thresholds, exhaustion state, arbitrary positive usage increments, automatic window rollover, dashboard/export status, and the pinned empty-history behavior. Native tracking is integrated through SharedStorage and WindowCounter rather than exposing Python's Redis-specific get_quota_usage/reset/get_all_quotas helpers; the pinned helper itself inconsistently mixes string keys and Redis hashes, and no production Python caller uses those paths.

backend-services/utils/rate_limit_simula.notes: Rust now provides the standalone offline simulator: uniform, burst, spike, gradual, and random traffic generation; Python's inclusive sliding-window limit and burst accounting; per-second peaks and aggregate statistics; rule comparisons; change previews; burst-effectiveness sweeps; reports and recommendations; named scenarios; and quick simulation. Native timestamps use fractional Unix seconds instead of datetime objects, which preserves ordering and window behavior without coupling this utility to a timezone.

backend-services/utils/rate_limiter.py.notes: Rust preserves thread-safe expiring memory counters, shared Redis atomic counters, disabled-rule bypass, fixed/current-window limits, Python's pre-increment remaining count, window reset/retry metadata, continuous token buckets, hybrid burst capacity, all tier minute/hour/day windows, 429 bodies, and rate-limit headers. Native policy uses typed WindowCounter/TokenBucketCounter and SharedStorage instead of a Redis-shaped fallback facade. Administrative per-rule reset/current-usage helpers are distributed across runtime state and quota routes, and the pinned hybrid algorithm's separate secondary burst-key behavior is approximated by a single token bucket, so this remains partial.

backend-services/utils/validation_util.p.notes: Rust loads enabled endpoint schemas, validates schema paths, resolves dotted and indexed fields, supports nested objects and typed arrays, preserves Python's bool-as-number behavior, exact range/pattern/enum/format error text, registered custom validators, and applies the same schema across REST, SOAP, GraphQL operation variables, and HTTP-to-gRPC messages. SOAP conversion is namespace-safe and rejects DTD/entities. Remaining differences are parser/runtime specific: Rust's GraphQL validation uses a bounded structural parser rather than graphql-core, and native gRPC validation consumes the gateway's JSON message shape rather than reflecting arbitrary Python protobuf objects.

backend-services/utils/redis_client.py.notes: Approved language/runtime replacement: the Python file is a redis-py connection-pool facade over generic Redis commands. Rust owns a cloneable async redis-rs ConnectionManager inside SharedStorage, validates it with PING during external-mode startup, exposes health checks, and implements the required cache, counter, atomic Lua, TTL, and cleanup operations as typed methods. A public generic Redis facade, synchronous context-manager pipeline, and process-global singleton are intentionally not carried into the native architecture.
backend-services/utils/redis_client.py.rationale: Python-specific synchronous redis-py adapter and singleton lifecycle are obsolete in the async native storage runtime; required Redis behavior is implemented through typed SharedStorage operations.

backend-services/utils/doorman_cache_uti.notes: Rust preserves every Python cache namespace and default TTL, JSON-native values (including restored byte wrappers), expiring memory/external Redis storage, chaos Redis failure injection, targeted policy invalidation, and privileged clearing of all gateway cache state. Native caches are typed SharedStorage operations rather than a process-global generic facade. Memory mode currently has no CACHE_MAX_SIZE LRU eviction or cache-info statistics, and async Redis writes are awaited rather than returned as executor futures.

backend-services/utils/constants.py.notes: Rust now defines every pinned header, pagination, multipart, permission, error-code, and message constant with the exact Python value. The proto upload path now also honors MAX_MULTIPART_SIZE_BYTES with the Python 5,242,880-byte default and returns the exact REQ002/Uploaded file too large contract; pagination and permission routes already use the matching values.

backend-services/utils/database.py.notes: Rust preserves memory/external mode selection, authenticated Mongo startup, dynamic collections, admin/role/group bootstrap defaults, typed CRUD and replacement, Python-compatible $or/$in memory filters, dotted and null-setting updates, UUID identities, async iteration equivalents, memory dump/restore, chaos failures, health/close lifecycle, and corrected Mongo unique/non-unique indexes including api_id, endpoint_id, tier_id/name, assignments, and vault entries. Python's synchronous PyMongo-shaped cursor/result wrapper classes and module-global collection aliases are obsolete in the async native runtime; memory bootstrap demo-log injection is not reproduced.

backend-services/utils/error_codes.py.notes: Rust now exposes the complete centralized error registry: all 161 named ErrorCode constants exactly match the pinned Python names and values, including the non-sequential and legacy wire codes. ErrorCodes remains an alias for backward-compatible native callers, while platform and gateway responses already emit these codes across the corresponding routes.

backend-services/utils/geo_lookup.py.notes: Rust now preserves the pinned placeholder lookup (cached UNKNOWN with 24-hour TTL), cached location fields, fail-open unknown/error policy, country block and allow lists, country-specific limits, exact access-denial reasons, sliding 24-hour country counters, sorted geographic distribution, and list retrieval. The native utility uses synchronized typed memory because the pinned module has no production callers; it can be replaced by an external GeoIP/storage provider without changing this contract.

backend-services/utils/ip_rate_limiter.p.notes: Rust preserves proxy-aware client-IP extraction, IPv4/IPv6 and CIDR allow/deny enforcement, forwarded-header precedence when explicitly trusted, fixed/sliding/token-bucket request limits, and expiring counters. Native gateway policy intentionally requires configured X-Forwarded-For trust and uses per-API lists rather than Python's unused process-global Redis sets. The standalone reputation score, automatic temporary bans, IP analytics/top-IP scan, and suspicious-activity helper are not yet implemented.

backend-services/services/gateway_servic.notes: Rust preserves API and endpoint resolution (including distinct GTW002/GTW003 failures), disabled/public/auth policy, CORS and preflight behavior, request identity and allowed-header forwarding, system/user credit precedence, authorization swapping, endpoint validation and transforms, client routing, timeouts, retries/backoff, circuit breaking, upstream status and malformed-JSON mapping, SOAP version and WS-Security processing, GraphQL depth/error handling, and descriptor-driven gRPC unary/client/server/bidirectional streaming with metadata filtering, TLS, limits, and status mapping. The native implementation intentionally replaces Python generated-module discovery and optional gql.Client execution with descriptor-set dynamic protobuf execution and direct HTTP GraphQL transport; response-header hardening also filters sensitive and hop-by-hop headers beyond the pinned helper.

backend-services/services/tier_service.p.notes: Rust preserves tier CRUD and idempotent creation, enabled filtering/pagination, pinned search failure behavior, assignment replacement/removal/listing, default and effective-date selection, override limits, deletion guards, upgrade/downgrade/temporary/trial/payment-failure transitions, both notification emails, comparisons, and per-tier/all-tier statistics. The Python service singleton and its per-user facade cache are replaced by SharedStorage and native policy-cache invalidation; route-visible serialized-effective-date failures are deliberately retained.

backend-services/utils/prometheus_metric.notes: Rust preserves enable/disable behavior, the exact histogram buckets and names, nonnegative duration observations, status labels, retry/timeout counters, and Prometheus text rendering; native output also exposes the additive active-request gauge.
